# Avora

> Avora is an open-source macOS screen recorder written in Swift with ScreenCaptureKit. It zooms in on every click, draws a smooth cursor, records microphone, system audio and camera, writes captions on the Mac and exports MP4, HEVC, ProRes or GIF.

Download Avora.zip from https://github.com/halitsever/avora-screen-recorder/releases/latest and move Avora to Applications. It needs macOS 14 or later and Screen Recording permission. Builds are signed ad hoc, so open it the first time with right-click, Open.

## Docs

- [Using Avora](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/#using): recording the screen, a window or an area, sound, camera, captions, keyboard badges and the editor
- [Automatic zoom](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/#zoom): how clicks become zooms and how the camera follows your work
- [Backgrounds](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/#backgrounds): no backdrop by default, gradients, colors, pictures and wallpaper
- [Install](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/#install): download, updates, building from source and re-rendering a recording from the command line
- [Under the hood](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/#hood): export settings, presets and the source layout
- [Screen Studio alternative](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/screen-studio-alternative): how Avora compares with Screen Studio, what they share and what Avora lacks
- [Mac screen recorder with audio](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/mac-screen-recorder-with-audio/): recording the microphone and system audio without BlackHole, features and a comparison with the built-in recorder, OBS and Screen Studio
- [Blog](https://projects.halit.org/avora-screen-recorder/blog/): guides to starting and stopping screen recordings on Mac, recording system audio and voice, where recordings are saved, OBS alternatives, GIF export and how auto zoom works
